Just like now, there was a military Campagnola leading the column, and I saw this for a fraction of a moment when there was this bend in the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: As I said, sir, you never mentioned this before. And there was testimony from a witness, and it was only after this testimony that you could possibly have learned about this. I'm positive that there was somebody who talked you into mentioning this Campagnola which you have never mentioned before?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I object to that question. I find it offensive. If it's trying to be suggested it's OTP, which it tends to be with my learned friend Mr. Borovic, that has not been the case whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, you may, if you think it is justified, put to a witness that their evidence is something that has not been previously spoken about or written about by that witness in previous evidence or in testimony. You may then wish to explore how it is that the witness now thinks of something that has not previously been mentioned. But to frame your question as this is framed carries a very clear indication that you are suggesting that there has been positive intervention to persuade this witness to mention a particular topic, and as Mr. Moore has indicated, the clear implication is who did that. Now, that is a very serious suggestion. If you have reason to support that, fine; but I think you may not have intended what is the effect of what you have said. And if that's the case, I would suggest that you should be very careful how you frame this sort of question in future because it creates an unnecessary and an undesirable impression. Now, I've been very muted and limited in what I've said, but please don't take that as being that I don't regard this as a serious matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, needless to say, I take everything you say as a serious matter and I accept all of your instructions. But if the other party sometimes refers to their own native legal system, then I have to refer to the legal system of the country that I come from, and that is encouraging the witness to give false testimony. There had been many border-line cases, so to speak, so far of this, at least in my definition of the term. But here we have a fact that's mentioned right here, right now for the very first time. I've told the witness so, and I've shown the witness his testimony from the Belgrade case where he said something totally different. I will now stop, and I will try to be more reserved with future witnesses, but it was high time I told a witness here before this Chamber that he should not start coming up with facts which he had never mentioned in any of his previous statements now of all places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, that is wrong. Let me make it very clear: Witnesses do remember things that they have not previously remembered, especially when they are asked about details that previous questioners and previous investigators have not inquired about. So just because a witness's evidence differs from something said before does not mean that this witness is manufacturing new evidence. Let that be first said. Where something new emerges in evidence, it may be that the witness is creating evidence. That is a matter which you may properly explore and which this Chamber is aware of and will be conscious of. But just because it happens that there is something you mentioned does not mean that the witness is creating evidence, manufacturing evidence. It's a perfectly normal, human occurrence. So don't firstly jump to the conclusion that it's false and it's about time you did something about it. The second thing is that you may properly explore with the witness why for the first time now the witness mentions something that has not been previously mentioned. But when you do that, unless you have some very specific basis, please avoid the trap of jumping to the conclusion that somebody has improperly persuaded the witness to do that. It may be very much the witness's own memory which, rightly or wrongly, has thought of something. Now, it's not a matter of different legal systems; it's a matter of ordinary human experience. Now, please understand that if you want to explore with this witness why it is that his evidence is different now from anything previously said, you may do it. But you don't do it by suggesting some improper conduct by other people, unless you have some sound basis for that. I hope it is now clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, I will comply with all your instructions. Even if I were not willing to, obviously I would still have to comply. There are mechanisms in place to ensure that. We broached the question of not granting a certain witness protective measures, if you remember. I believe that has something to do with this particular testimony. When that happens, the Trial Chamber will see for itself that this person told enormous lies about things that have been the matter of evidence before this Court. I will, however, now stop and proceed to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, you are bordering now on extremely improper conduct. May I suggest for your own sake that you stop making that sort of assertion at this point in these proceedings. And if you return to questioning this witness about his evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. You are very kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My next question: When you came to The Hague to testify for the first time, who did you go with?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: It had been a long time. And if memory serves me, with Dr. Vesna Bosanac and another lady doctor who was a dentist.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you all together in Zagreb before you left?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anyone from the defence ministry prepare you for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I know of, not over the last 15 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said in reference to one of the persons you identified from the list, Ivan Kovac, that he worked with the post office to the very last day, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were the phone lines in good working order all the way until the 17th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The phone lines at the time in Vukovar had long been down, as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that Ivan Kovac could not possibly have gone about his regular job? And what was it that he was doing to the very last day there if the phone lines were down?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The phone lines in the town of Vukovar itself were down, but I don't know about the technology being used now or what he was doing. He wasn't the one who told me. It was his dad who told me after the liberation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This person you identified as Kuhar; I think that's number 21, isn't it? My question in relation to this person is: Is this person still alive, or is this person listed as missing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This person is no longer alive. He was with me at Ovcara. He was a young man from Nasice or somewhere near Nasice. He had no parents; he was an orphan. And I wanted to give him a proper burial. I remember him because his shoe size was 48. He came to my warehouse to get a pair of shoes and I couldn't provide one, and that's why I remember. He was an orphan. He didn't have a mother or a father, but he has a brother who still receives financial compensation from the Croatian state because his brother is still listed as missing and has never been found. This is what some of my friends from Nasice told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean he's still listed as missing and his brother is receiving his pension, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Something you said about the list yesterday, you said you wrote down the names that you did. And after that you said: Additionally, I remember two other names that I shared with Their Honours. And probably you meant the Prosecutor, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But after that you said: Additionally, I told him about those two names.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After you compiled the list, you never talked to anyone else again until you appeared in this courtroom, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My last question. My question is: Did you hear that in the Croatian defence ministry there is a special unit preparing witnesses to testify here in The Hague? Have you ever heard of the existence of such a unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was never prepared by anyone for my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone wasn't on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Berghofer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm Novak Lukic, and on behalf of the Defence team for Veselin Sljivancanin, I'm going to ask you a few questions. I didn't want to interfere with my colleague Borovic's cross-examination, but I believe that on page 46, lines 5 and 6 need to be corrected. If you want an explanation of this, we should move into private session.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Leave it until after your cross-examination, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Berghofer, you listened to questions put to you by my colleagues, and we would like to make this cross-examination as expeditious as possible, and we decided to divide the topics amongst ourselves. So I'm going to refer to topics that Mr. Vasic didn't ask you about, the barracks and the hospital, on the 18th and the 20th November. And I'll ask you a couple of questions about Velepromet and the barracks after you returned from Ovcara. Let me just remind you once again of the fact that it would be a good idea to allow for a short pause after my question, a couple of seconds, because otherwise it's very difficult for the interpreters to follow if we both speak at the same time, and in that case the transcript is no good either. First of all, I will ask you a couple of questions about my own custom before I move on to talk about the hospital, a general question that I normally put to all witnesses. You gave evidence, as you yourself have said, to -- on a number of occasions before various trials and courts, et cetera. And I believe that everything you said tallies on one point, that is to say, that after the conversation between Sljivancanin and Dr. Ivankovic that you've described to us, that is to say, after you were boarded on to buses at the hospital on the 20th of November, after that you have never ever seen my client again. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to specify it once again. At Ovcara barracks, at Modateks, at Velepromet, and then again at the barracks, and at Sremska Mitrovica, you have never seen Mr. Sljivancanin in any of those places. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put to you another question relating to the period prior to your arrival at the hospital, something that came to me when you were answering questions by my colleague Mr. Vasic yesterday. You said that you were familiar with the combat operations in the area of Sajmiste. I'm going to ask you about a short episode there, if you remember that. Maybe you could describe it. If you don't remember, we can move on. What I'm referring to is the following: Do you have any recollection at all of the attempt of an arrival of a convoy of doctors on the 13th of October when from the direction of Negoslavci they were trying to reach the hospital in order to bring medical supplies and take over patients and near Sajmiste they were stopped by the Croat defence lines. And that is to say, Mr. Borkovic, a member of the Jastrebs, prevented the convoy from getting through because he was afraid that the JNA tanks might follow in their wake. Do you remember anything at all in conjunction with this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection of anything like that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can you confirm that the route from Sajmiste to the centre of town was mined and that there were obstacles and barricades in the street and they were mined as well? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I left Sajmiste either on the 24th or on the 25th of August, and I never went back until seven years later. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The shelter where you were which you described to Vasic yesterday, how far is it from the hospital, in your estimation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 8 to 900 metres, four bus-stops, roughly speaking. Maybe -- I'm talking about ten cellars there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've already told me that you left Sajmiste as early as August, so presumably you will be unable to answer the following question but I will put it to you anyway, as it is my duty. Do you know anything about the events in the beginning of October when a combat vehicle was attacked, when five soldiers were kidnapped, and they were buried near Radnicko Naselje and the others who survived had been taken to hospital? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we can move to the events at the hospital starting from the moment when you got there. As you told us, you arrived at the hospital around midnight on the 17th of November. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After you decided you would not go for the breakthrough, do you go to the hospital straight away or did you spend time in town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no town. It's the cemetery, the Sloga football stadium, and then the hospital. I went straight to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the entire group, everybody who was with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think there were six of us in all -- or maybe five, six, seven -- six probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't need to go into any great detail, but let me just remind you that you initially said there were eight of you in a statement you gave to the OTP. Maybe it's a mistake?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can easily give you the names of the people even now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've already told us; no need.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did the other members of the group carry arms as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The people who were with me did not have any weapons. I was the only one who had an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: De facto you mentioned the names of several doctors as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One doctor and his wife, Marko Mandic, who was the plaster technician, and I think his wife as well. As far as I can remember, it was his wife and myself, and Njofra Jankovic who was Gretel's son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We had evidence before this Court according to which the plaster technician, Marko Mandic, was putting plaster-casts on the legs of soldiers or people who engaged in combat operations in order to feign injuries. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I know Manko [as interpreted] Mandic by sight, but I have no idea what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, it is my duty to put the question to you. So you see how much time is needed in order for what we are saying to appear on the transcript. Just tell me in a few words - you don't have to explain everything in any great detail - but starting from the time when you arrived there on the 17th you said that you must have spent time in the basement until you went to Dr. Ivankovic's office. Did you move about in the course of those two days? Did you walk around the corridors, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was carrying water.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard that civilians who started arriving at the hospital in large numbers mostly went to the upper floors. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole hospital was packed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see Mrs. Vesna Bosanac at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very difficult to get to see her, but I did see her between the 17th and the 18th, thereabouts. I can't tell you exactly at what time, but I did see her, only once there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did she herself or anyone else tell you that Vesna Bosanac was against the civilians getting to the hospital? She was of the view that they should go to the collection centre at Velepromet. Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in the course of those few days lists of civilians had been compiled by Ljerka Zgonjanin from the Red Cross and Marin Vidic [as interpreted] from the Red Cross as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that and Dragica Tuskan as well. My name was taken down three times by Ljerka Zgonjanin. She's from Patkovici, but she was a self-proclaimed Red Cross employee. There was nothing really official there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did Dr. Ivankovic, in the course of your conversation perhaps, tell you that civilians should move to Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Dr. Ivankovic perhaps mention that the ZNG and the defenders troops were putting on white coats or putting on plaster-casts or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now we shall move on to my client's conversation with Dr. Ivankovic -- or rather, a monologue, as you said, on the morning of the 20th, as far as I understood it, around 7.00?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not trying to put any leading questions to you. What time was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 7.30. Okay, let's say it was 7.30. It was in the morning anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. Tell me where you were prior to witnessing their meeting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no meeting. I was being escorted by Ivankovic, and we were shaking hands. And at that juncture he came along from somewhere and he shouted: Doctor, what are we waiting for? I've already said this in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was my understanding of the situation. But what I'm particularly interested in - and this is something that you said to my colleague from the Prosecution as well - is that you were greeting Ivankovic at that stage. Why?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was high time for me to get out of the hospital to see what was going on, because there were had been vehicles coming and going throughout the night so we were saying good-bye. And I suppose that I, too, would be taken away somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you were parting company, as it were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat my client's sentence once again, but very slowly for the sake of the transcript. I was slightly sceptical the first time round. So just in order to avoid any misunderstanding, what did he tell Dr. Ivankovic at that stage?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Doctor, what are we waiting for? We are at war. Lightly wounded and the civilians should go to the left and medical staff to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There's one thing that didn't get into the transcript. He said: We're at war. Didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think "state of war" should be better than "we're at war." It's a piece of advice for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you on that morning -- and I would like to go back to where you were. I suppose you had spent the night in Dr. Ivankovic's office. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that particular night, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And prior to you saying good-bye to Ivankovic, had you already come out into the corridor, out of that office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you said good-bye to him in the office?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, just outside. Perkovic and myself, I don't know whether I've mentioned him, but the two of us were leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear any of the names being called, any roll-call for people to come out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear previously that doctors and medical staff had been -- had been called to attend the meeting at the plaster room?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was the plaster room, I remember that they were looking for Dr. Ivankovic and that he left us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And this conversation with Sljivancanin took place after you parted with Dr. Ivankovic or at that precise moment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was earlier, much earlier. And this fact when he said: We are at war, was on the 20th in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you didn't hear that anyone was being convened to a meeting at the plaster room on the 20th in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that. Perhaps he might have been invited to attend the meeting, but I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to this column which was formed, these people who were searched later on and led to the buses, could you tell me whether you were, rather, at the start, in the middle, or at the end of the column of those, roughly speaking, 250 people, as you said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe in the middle. I couldn't see the beginning or the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you described the appearance of my client and how you managed to recognise him later, he [as interpreted] said that he had a military cap, a camouflage uniform, a bullet-proof vest, and a moustache, and he was a tall man?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On that occasion -- or throughout your stay at the hospital and also on the occasion when you were leaving the hospital, did you see any people who were also officers or were wearing similar clothes to the one he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I only saw younger soldiers and the reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: An that occasion - and I'm referring to the conversation which took place outside Dr. Ivankovic's office - did you see any other doctors from the Vukovar medical centre that you knew at that moment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you were in the office prior to that, I am unable to ask you the following question, so will you just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to be shown his statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the same set of statements that you have been shown by Mr. Vasic. It's something to do with this particular portion of your testimony. Let us now please go back to your statement to the Vinkovci magistrate on the 7th of March, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to assist my learned friends from the OTP -- just a minute, please. The English reference -- just a minute, please. Page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The B/C/S page, which is a language that we understand, could you please go to page 3 -- page 2, rather, midway down the page. Paragraph 3, the really big one. I will read something that's there in the middle, and you can confirm if that's what you said. "Pursuant to instructions from this major, the civilians were separated from the rest. The six buses were first taken to the JNA barracks." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Either this is not something that you referred to at the time or the magistrate failed to record the "slightly wounded and medical staff."

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have a rough idea what I'm saying, but if you have a look at the document you should know better.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the OTP. The B/C/S reference is 00537419.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is how the paragraph begins: "At 7.00 in the morning" -- can you see that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to read that out for you slowly and you can just check as I go along?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "7.00 in the morning on the 20th of November, 1991, when the hospital was already half empty I saw a man I identified as Sljivancanin yelling at Dr. Ivankovic: What are we waiting for? We are at war. He also said that on our way out of the hospital the civilians should go to one side and the slightly wounded to the other. When we left the hospital and lined up in the courtyard outside, Sljivancanin changed his mind and sent the medical staff to the right and the rest of us to the left." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was listening to you. If that's what it says, then I will take your word for it gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question to you now in relation to what you testified here and what you said to the OTP in chief: His words, according to you, were: The slightly wounded and civilians to the left, and the rest --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And medical staff to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether at this time while you were on your way out of the hospital you actually saw how many medical staff were on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This wasn't something that one could see, Mr. Lukic. They took the main entrance facing Lola Ribar Street, that's the hospital's main entrance. And we took the side entrance, facing south.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After he said this, do you remember what Dr. Ivankovic said or did?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Said to me, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear him say anything at all? Did you hear him talk to Sljivancanin or what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing. I don't remember him saying anything at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see if he - and I mean Dr. Ivankovic - issued any instructions to you or any of the staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no one near us, Mr. Lukic. I left and went to the hospital courtyard; it's right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This Chamber has a high degree of familiarity with the various photographs and the general appearance of the entire area, as well as the emergency exit, what we usually term the emergency exit, where the corridor was, and there was the exit facing Gunduliceva Street. Did you see Major Sljivancanin anywhere in that particular area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was only while I was still outside that I saw: Everybody should get on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the only thing you heard him say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't even have time to look at him. He was turning around, and what do I know? We had been lined up and checked by this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you've said that already. Thank you. You knew, and that was your testimony too, that those civilians who had nothing to do brought no relation to the medical staff or the wounded had been taken on trucks to Velepromet the previous evening?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous night, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you were neither medical staff nor wounded, nor did you have anything to do with the hospital, why did you go to Velepromet, too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Dr. Ivankovic told him: You just sit it out until tomorrow morning, and then you'll be leaving tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were hiding in his office, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We weren't exacting hiding, but there were about 10, 12, or 14 of us in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The JNA arrived on the afternoon of the 19th; you described that for us, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were a civilian who had previously discarded his rifle under a car that was nearby?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A burnt-out shell of a car, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was a breakthrough attempt on your part?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You had no uniform on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you were not one of those people who were supposed to be at the hospital; rather, you were supposed to go to Velepromet, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One didn't know at the time who would go where. Everybody flocked to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you heard the trucks and you realised that all the floors were being emptied and that civilians were being taken to Velepromet throughout that night, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite honest, I didn't see but I could hear the roar of trucks taking people away throughout the night. There was a nurse there probably who dropped a hint or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You must have known at the time, at least based on whatever rumours circulated around the hospital, there were people among the wounded who were pretending to be among the wounded and sick, who were passing themselves off as wounded?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about this because I didn't budge from my room for the whole night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the next day when you headed for the buses and when let me say you were at the barracks and Ovcara, did you see any persons in white overcoats who you knew for sure not to be medical staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Samardzic was, but he had been working for the hospital, too, for the last two months before Vukovar fell. I have no idea what exactly he was doing there. I met him once when I was at the hospital, not just to see Dr. Ivankovic. I was giving out cigarette lighters to the wounded, both Croats and Serbs alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if, perhaps, he worked with the hospital security detail?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That morning outside Ivankovic's office, as you were walking up and down the corridor, did you perhaps see --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean if I saw --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I haven't finished my question yet.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see any doctors wearing military uniforms checking patients?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Beside me, or behind me, for that matter, Mr. Lukic, the only persons there were the two Dosen brothers. One of them was lying on a stretcher and the other was walking past. Martin Dosen, the boxer, I think was the wounded one on the stretcher; and the tall one, the other one, was walking past and -- but he had saliva dribbling down his chin. Excuse my French.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the rest of them who weren't wounded had nothing on them to show that they were in fact not to be classed among the wounded, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to the extent I was able to tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were I to tell you that at the time you have specified my client would not have been able to talk to Dr. Ivankovic because they were both at the meeting in the plaster room, which was in a different room down the same corridor that you were walking up and down, and they were actually seen there by some witnesses whose testimony we have heard, you would probably say I'm wrong, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you hold me to that very second when everything happened, it might be my mistake as well, but believe me, I'm not trying to blame Sljivancanin by saying this. It was in passing that he yelled this. Maybe he was on his way to that very meeting. What knows? But that's what he said: Doctor, what are we waiting for? We are at war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you a while ago and -- well, that at least was my understanding. You did not see any people with the hospital IDs who were taken to one side?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was among those -- or I was with some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember them remaining outside the bus, the five of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well now, after the frisking in the tunnel outside the emergency ward, how long did you remain standing there, and how long did you take to get from the emergency ward to the bus? How long do you think that took you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just over an hour, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you only briefly saw Sljivancanin for a moment, as you have described, when he said that all the persons there should be boarded on the buses, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he just walked off to the left [as interpreted] doing that military step and he said everybody should get on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said in one of your statements - I'll have to look for it but perhaps you can challenge that I'm saying - the witness --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can't hear the witness. We believe the microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Correction, on page 63, page -- line 25 the witness said: "Off to the right" and the transcript says: "Off to the left."

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, who went left and who went right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's just a correction for the transcript. You went to the left and he went to the right, right, isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was standing there already. I had been frisked by this time, and he was on his way out from the hospital going to the right, walking towards the hospital staff, going towards Lola Ribar Street and not stopping.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. We have heard testimony before this Court that a colonel was there who gave orders for people to start boarding the buses. Also, you said I believe in one of your statements to the OTP, but if that is not true we'll go and look for it, perhaps if you challenge what I'm about to say, he allegedly told his deputy that people should start getting on the buses. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about that man? Was he wearing camouflage uniform, too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't, Mr. Lukic. He was wearing the regular reserve JNA uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were on the buses before the buses took off, how long were you there for, on the buses?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20 minutes, I'd say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I understand your testimony, as one by one the buses were filled, people -- the buses would move along and the people would get on the next bus in line, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was no order given by anybody for some people to go to one bus and some other people to go to another, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I noticed or heard anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to read back to you a portion of your testimony at the Belgrade trial. This is the 25th of October. There's a copy of the transcript for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of my learned friends, the transcript page, the English, page 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For you, Witness, it's page 73. It's the 25th. There are two versions of the transcript, and the 25th, the one dated the 25th from the Belgrade trial is the one I'm talking about. Page 73. Mr. Berghofer, the buses that you said had Zrenjanin license plates on them, were those civilian buses and what was their colour?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Lukic, but they were civilian buses, rather small, not the really big ones. Medium size, I'd say. Not particularly big or particularly small.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And they all looked alike, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very much so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm reading from page 73 down towards the bottom of the page. Dragoljub Todorovic, counsel for Croatian victims at the Belgrade trial asked you the following question: "As for the events at the hospital you said: Sljivancanin called over this man Ivankovic and said: These people should go there and those other people should go here." And then you go on to say: "Throughout this time Sljivancanin was the main commander there." My question to you is: Based on what did you reach this conclusion that he was the main commander there? And your answer is - I'm about to read it to you -- that was the question. And the answer was: Witness victim Berghofer: "I didn't say that he was the main man there. He just said: Well, look, Sljivancanin is the kind of man you could spot from miles away; that's how tall he was." And then the counsel asks you another question: "In order to ask you an accurate question, I'll rephrase. You said that he was the main commander there at the hospital. My question is: Based on what did you reach that particular conclusion?" Your answer, sir: "Look, now, I didn't know who that man was. He was wearing a flak jacket and uniform. I didn't see his rank. How on earth would I have recognised him? He was just there as doctor and I were on our way out. He came in and said: Doctor, what are we waiting for? We are at war. The slightly wounded and the rest that I've said and the civilians to the left to Sapudl, and that's all I know about the man." Witness, I have just read back to you what you stated at the trial there. So my question, based on what you've just heard, this is what you stated at the Belgrade trial, and that was your testimony some minutes ago. You had the distinct impression that he was the main man there, that he was exercising command, based on what he told Dr. Ivankovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall now move on to the barracks and the events that took place there. You mentioned before this Trial Chamber the arrival to the barracks and the fact that the buses were parked in a semicircle. Did you on any previous occasion enter the perimeter of the Vukovar barracks? Do you know where the barracks is situated within this entire perimeter?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I was only 12 metres away from the perimeter myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These buses that were parked in a semicircle, how far were they from the main building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that they were pretty far, according to my recollection. It is a bit difficult to tell you exactly after so many years, but maybe up to 50, 60 metres, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On a parking lot?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to show two photos to the witness. This is something new, and I believe that it would be of interest to all of us to see what the barracks looked like. We received these pictures when we visited Vukovar from the Defence ministry of the Republic of Croatia -- actually, we received them only very recently. These photos have been disclosed to the Prosecution, so they are familiar with them. I would like to show the witness these two photos, and I would also like the Trial Chamber to see the outline which shows a sketch, and it tells us from what point precisely the photos were taken. It would be easier for you to have a full picture of what the barracks was like. The first picture, picture 2D100009.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berghofer, are you familiar with this place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It has changed since, but this is the side facing Negoslavci and the first part should be different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise something?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes. I think this is the barracks, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please take your Magic Marker and show it to us.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, it's these two buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please indicate the barracks building by number 1.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not so clear-cut. Here to the right there is a kind of copes [phoen] and some cars are parked here and there is some more shrubbery here, and I can't see it properly. I don't know from what side this picture was taken. If it was taken from the direction of my house, I can't really remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you like it to be blown up?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The perspective is somewhat weird. I think it will probably say that the dentist's surgery is somewhere -- and I actually grew up there. If this is the barracks, yes, okay, 1, 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we take a look at another picture and then we'll come back to this.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the picture marked 2D100002.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise anything here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just hang on a second. You keep showing me the wrong side. That's not where we came in. What is this to the right, this big building? Can you help me out?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to know, too. And you don't seem to know, and I haven't lived there myself. Can we look at the next picture?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it, that's more like it. This is the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we see on this picture?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, this is the road to Negoslavci, and this is the side entrance for lorries coming into the barracks. It's not the front gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, is this where you came in on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic. We came from the direction of Negoslavci. Presumably this is the gate then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't like anything to be marked on this picture in particular, but can you please admit it into evidence on the basis of what the witness has said, that this is the entrance to the barracks where they came in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's from the direction of Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you help me, please, Mr. Berghofer. Is that a photograph taken from inside the barracks looking out or from outside the barracks looking in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, from inside looking out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is the road that passes from the left side to the right side the road to Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the road into town, according to this picture, and to the left is the road to Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So to the right of the picture is the town, Vukovar, and to the left is Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You tender this photograph, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D232.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have another picture, 2D100004.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does this area ring a bell? Can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I can see is parking areas, garages.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And where are these parking spaces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the perimeter of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is what I'm most interested in. In relation to these garages and in relation to the barracks, can you tell us how far those buses, five or six buses, parked in a semicircle were from these garages?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it is very difficult to tell at this moment. If this indeed is the parking area for the tanks that I could see on occasion from my own house, because I lived nearby, in my view the picture or -- perhaps not the picture, but the road leading up to the office area should be somewhere here because we came through and entered the secondary courtyard of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That, I understand. But as far as I can tell on the basis of what you've said, you were about 50 to 60 metres away from the barracks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't want to have this entered into the evidence for the moment because it is not, strictly speaking, necessary. And I don't know whether to go into the map now. Perhaps if we could show 2D100001 to the witness just for a moment. Could you blow it up a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I must tell you, Mr. Berghofer, that it is not very clear to me but can you see anything at all on this plan? In that case, you could perhaps tell us where you were; but if not, maybe not.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just try and understand this thing. Can you tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says the Sapudl Street on top.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that you were showing me the barracks. That's what we were talking about. I do apologise. I didn't realise --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I do apologise. It's not Sapudl. It says "Sajmiste" in the upper right corner.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's too small, I can't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can't either.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, Sajmiste. But Sajmiste is very big. And now number 2, what is number 2? Is it supposed to be the main gate to the barracks? Perhaps it's the side entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The street to the right is the Sanja Marinkovic Street.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the former Yugoslavia there was no Sanja Marinkovic Street. That street does not exist. If it was to the right, it is Dr. Mladen Stojanovic Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what we were given by the Croatian authorities, but never mind. We won't dwell on this picture any longer. We will try and show it to another witness who might be able to clarify it a little bit. Let's move to the events in the barracks now. When the buses arrived and were parked in this semicircle, those TO people, volunteers, paramilitaries, reservists, all sorts of them, well, how much later did they appear? Were they already there or did they come along later on, after 15 minutes or 30 minutes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, they had a party as soon as we came in. They were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, this show of hatred or anger when you were still on the buses, did it go on for all of the four hours that you spent there or did they withdraw at any point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, they did not withdraw at all, but some of them were absent. But the others went on circling around the buses and sometimes -- something else that I didn't say because nobody asked me about it, but they said they had flags and they were furious outside. But the -- they were prevented from coming in by the young soldier who was on the bus, and it went on for about 20 minutes as far as I can remember. But the others, they were going crazy outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we just be specific about this. Those attempts on their part to enter the buses went on for 20 hours [as interpreted] and all of that time they were going crazy outside, as you say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. They were shouting and jumping and threatening and you know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it went on throughout those four hours that you spent at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. Can I continue so I'll explain you how it went?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You may continue, but what I want to know is this fact --

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them smashed the fire extinguishers, others took implements such as rakes and spades and shovels. And then they took some people on a bus in the direction of Negoslavci and then a group of them, five to six of them, boarded one Yugo car and drove behind the bus to Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You've already said that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what about the rest of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the rest of them were still going crazy outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think that at 73, line 16, it should be 20 minutes, not 20 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just take a look? Yes, absolutely, it's 20 minutes. [In English] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You testified now and throughout your testimony you said that those young soldiers who escorted your buses prevented anyone from assaulting you directly, that is to say, from boarding the buses. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, several people got off your bus. You mentioned Kolesar, Professor Licina and Hidek. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if their names were called, read out from a list, or how did it happen? How did it come about? Did somebody get on the bus and ask them to get off or were they taken away in another way? I'm interested in those three men.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, as far as I can remember, one reservist, a youngish man, came and said: Well, Professor, how come you're there? And I don't know what the other guy answered. And he took him out, and he took out Hidek and Nurse Biba's husband, Kolesar, and they were all on my bus, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But do you remember anyone getting on the bus and calling their names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no. Nobody read out any names, any lists, anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps that Professor Licina sitting in the front seat together with his wife?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Mr. Lukic, he was ahead of me, maybe two lines of seats ahead of me, two rows ahead of me, but I can't remember that he was with his wife. I can't remember his wife, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the OTP and he said he was never taken off in the barracks but only at Ovcara. Could it be a case of confusion on your part that Professor Licina was first taken off the bus together with his wife at Ovcara but not before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I happen to know Professor Licina quite well. Nobody took anybody off the bus at Ovcara. Only that young soldier took Vili Karlovic off the bus that I was on. They knew each other or he had friends in Ruma and Pazova - don't let me go any further into that - but I can tell you that the young soldier saved the young lad's life.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Kolesar is the husband of Nurse Biba, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you are certain Licina was the man who got off the bus at the barracks, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Rudolf Vilhelm?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember him on your bus?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, no, he wasn't on my bus. But now you're probably likely to tell me again: But you didn't say that. And Bulidza was saying something like: What's the matter, Ruca? No more football, is there? It was as if Ruca was two or three ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember Ruca getting was on the second or the third bus? Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. Then when we met up he told me that he had also been at the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go briefly into private session for just one question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a bit of interpretation that seems confusing now. I asked you about Vilhelm Rudolf a while ago. If you can just please repeat. You said you saw him later on and he told you that he had been at the barracks, too. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His nickname is Ruca, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the break now, Your Honours? It's convenient for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Lukic. Now, you mentioned earlier a concern about some lines. As the transcript then read, you mentioned page 48, lines 5 and 6. And the transcript said you -- that it -- thought needed to be corrected. I've been advised that you may have meant page 46, lines 5 and 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you may have suggested redaction instead of correction. And I thought I'd let you know that I have ordered redaction. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are entirely right, Your Honour. You are reading my mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because of the redaction, we must have a 30-minute break with the tapes. So we will resume at five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Berghofer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll try to finish as quickly as possible and try to be as brief as possible for that very reason, but we still must make pauses between our questions and our answers. One question I forgot to ask you at the beginning, briefly, please, you described the breakthrough, how you left on the evening of the 18th. You passed the -- what used to be the old TO building. You just found a teleprinter there, right, you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was actually a command post for the TO, used to be?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it used to be a recruitment office in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is: What is the distance between that building and the hospital? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That building is number 7, and the hospital is number 47, about 200 metres apart, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll be asking you some questions in relation to Ovcara, Velepromet, and the barracks, just to check a number of persons related to these events, and then we can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll limit this just to people who are subject to problems? Yes. All right. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said you walked from Modateks to Velepromet, and you were led by Jezdimir Stankovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he wearing military uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You knew him from before, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you about some persons now. I won't be showing you the statement, but they were mentioned in that official note that the police officer took from you which you say you didn't sign. I will ask you the following, however. Did you mention to that police officer -- or rather, did you see at Velepromet a man by the name of Vlado Djitko?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was within the perimeter of Velepromet. I saw him as I was walking around. He is my former wife's cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was wearing a JNA military uniform, too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What -- how old was he? What do you reckon?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He might have been about 27 or 28 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also saw Seman Djurika?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was an apprentice of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform in Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He is Pavlovic's son-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us his age?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have been born in 1946 or 1948. I had just left the army, and he came to become an apprentice. There were perhaps four years in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Pavlovic, what about Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a stonemason. He helped with my house. I saw him at Modateks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he also wearing a JNA uniform?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, in Modateks. You got that? Yes. He was in uniform, standing guard there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about Pero Krtinic? Did you see him at Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I did, Mr. Lukic. I still see the image as if this happened only two days ago. He was jumping with joy when they brought me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was he wearing some sort of uniform, too?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I repeat this, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was wearing a uniform. And when he saw me, he started jumping for joy, and he said: Men like these, men like Drago, these are the men that we ought to kill. I summed enough courage to say: And for what reason? Our mothers had been neighbours for 40 years. You know what? He was suddenly lost for words. He said nothing at all. He was totally dumbfounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All these persons that I have listed are persons that you saw in Modateks and Velepromet. These people are Serbs, people who were not prisoners there, but rather were guarding you in Modateks and Velepromet?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not guarding. They were just there doing something, who knows what? Both Djitko and Seman are Ruthenians, not Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But they were all wearing JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they were not anywhere in our vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You knew these people from before because they were natives of Vukovar like you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All these people were wearing the same uniforms as those soldiers standing outside the so-called room of death, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were a little older, and outside the room of death there were two young soldiers. So the uniforms looked fresher, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There's no doubt about that. You described the soldiers standing outside the room of death as young soldiers and you didn't know them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And they had cleaner or fresher looking uniforms than those other ones?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was some degree of difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was because they seemed younger and you didn't know them, and because of their fresh uniforms you believed them to be regular JNA soldiers. Is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please briefly go back into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday while testifying in chief, we are now moving to the last segment of your testimony, as it were, the barracks after Velepromet where you were taken before you were off to Sremska Mitrovica. You described an incident, if I may call it that. You were first fed because you hadn't eaten in a long time, and then - and I took this down verbatim - you said: While you were asleep you heard sounds of people being hit and moans. You said that as far as you remembered that was your neighbour, Silt, but you didn't yourself see this person being beaten by anyone. So my question to you is: Is that what you said, first of all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This room, the entire group that I mentioned a while ago, that entire group of people, please don't say their names, were you all in that same room in the barracks before your journey to Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: For some reason I seem to remember that Vili Karlovic wasn't there, but I'm not sure, and then some other people came from somewhere else. But let's assume that Cakalic, myself, Guncevic, and someone else - who was it? - were there, but I'm not sure about Vili Karlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There's a correction. Page 84, line 7, it says the barracks of Velepromet, whereas I said: When they were taken from Velepromet to the barracks. I don't think that this is in dispute anyway. This room in which you were being kept, how large was it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I didn't really notice, but it was quite large. The way I'm picturing it now, there was some sort of a corridor and a room, but I'm stuck for the exact image right now and it's difficult to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just let it be then. You didn't ask this man called Silt whether anyone had beaten him or who had beaten him? That's what you said, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you exchange comments with any other of your fellow sufferers, to put it that way, about his beating, as it were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment we got to Mitrovica, Silt was taken somewhere else to Serbia, and it was later on that I found out from him -- I asked him: Were you the one who got a drubbing back there, and he said yes. But that was after the liberation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you didn't hear it from him on that occasion on that day or on the way to Sremska Mitrovica or in Mitrovica itself, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All of your memories about those days in Vukovar were the subject of your testimony twice before this Tribunal. You testified in Belgrade, you testified before the investigating magistrate in Zagreb, the investigating magistrate in Vinkovci, you gave a statement to the police in Croatia, and you gave statements to the OTP. Up until now -- or rather, yesterday in this courtroom you never mentioned this to anyone else, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for sure, but as far as I know nobody ever told me that I was not supposed to talk about testifying in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about this man called Silt? Did he display any physical signs of having been beaten the next morning when you were heading for Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. We said our good-byes very quickly. Some people's names were called out, and these people were then taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm now moving on to my last set of questions. I'll try to be as brief as possible. It's more by way of a conclusion based on everything that I have heard from you, so please try to confirm this, sir. You provided a detailed account of the mistreatment that you were subjected to at Ovcara before this Tribunal. You described the mental torture, too, and you described what you suffered at Velepromet. Did you suffer any mental or physical mistreatment or even did you receive any threats while you were at the hospital, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Aside from the threats outside the bus, were you subjected to any physical or mental mistreatment while you were in the barracks when those soldiers were guarding you on the bus?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In actual fact, throughout the time you were being guarded by the military police officers no harm came your way. Could I say that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, roughly speaking, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have very few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Throughout your time from being taken on the bus through the barracks and Ovcara, did you -- or did you see anybody receive any medical treatment or assistance for their injuries?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself did not receive any medical treatment, but I do remember this one man who felt extremely sick. He had been vomiting the whole night. I later realised that this man was Guncevic, but I didn't know that at the time, if that's what you mean. I myself requested nothing in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Did you see anybody receiving any medical treatment when they were at Ovcara and being beaten?

utterances.speaker: DRAGUTIN BERGHOFER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I am not certain that this arises out of the Defence's cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Provision of medical assistance, anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
